steps: Step 1, Count a group: draw 14 stars in two rows, 10 in the top row and 4 in the bottom. Touch each star once and say 1, 2, 3 up to 14, moving each touched star aside so none is counted twice.

Step 2, Write the number: 14 is one ten and four ones, so write 1 then 4. Say it aloud as fourteen. Compare with 41, which has the digits swapped but means four tens and one one, a much bigger number.
Step 3, Order numbers: put 9, 17, 12 and 5 in order from smallest to biggest. Look at each on a number line from 0 to 20. The order is 5, 9, 12, 17, because each one sits further right.
Step 4, Find the missing number: in the pattern 11, 12, __, 14, 15 count on from 12. The next count word is thirteen, so the gap is 13. Check by counting the whole row again from 11 to 15.
Step 5, Compare two numbers: which is more, 16 or 19? Count to 16 first, then keep going 17, 18, 19. Since 19 comes later in the count, 19 is more than 16, and 16 is less than 19.
Step 6, Your turn: draw 18 dots and write the number. Then put 7, 20, 13 and 2 in order from smallest to biggest. Answer: 18 is one ten and eight ones, and the order is 2, 7, 13, 20.
Step 1, Count in tens: touch ten-sticks one at a time and say 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Five sticks of ten make 50. Each jump adds one whole ten, so the ones digit stays 0 every time.
Step 2, Tens and ones: show 3 ten-sticks and 7 loose cubes. Three tens are 30, and 7 more makes 37. Write 3 in the tens place and 7 in the ones place, and say thirty-seven.
Step 3, Read a number: 64 has a 6 in the tens place and a 4 in the ones place. So it is 6 tens and 4 ones, which is 60 and 4. Draw 6 sticks and 4 cubes to prove it.
Step 4, Count on from a number: start at 47 and count on ones: 48, 49, 50. After 49 the ones run out, so we make a new ten and the number becomes 50. Then 51, 52 follow.
Step 5, Check on a hundred square: find 58 in the fifth row of tens. Going one step right gives 59, and one step down gives 68, ten more. This confirms that moving down adds a ten.
Step 6, Your turn: show 52 with sticks and cubes, then say how many tens and ones. Count on from 96 to 100. Answer: 52 is 5 tens and 2 ones, and the count is 97, 98, 99, 100.
Step 1, Add with objects: 6 red counters and 5 blue counters. Push them together and count all: 6, then 7, 8, 9, 10, 11. So 6 + 5 = 11. Writing it as a sentence helps: six and five make eleven.
Step 2, Count on with a number line: for 8 + 4 start on 8 and hop 4 times: 9, 10, 11, 12. Land on 12, so 8 + 4 = 12. Keep the bigger number in your head and count only the small one.
Step 3, Use number bonds to 10: 7 + 5. Split 5 into 3 and 2. Since 7 + 3 = 10, add the remaining 2 to get 12. So 7 + 5 = 12. Bonds to 10 make big sums easy.
Step 4, Check with doubles: 6 + 6 = 12 is a double. Then 6 + 7 is one more than the double, which is 13. A different route lets you confirm the earlier answers are sensible.
Step 5, Word problem: Amal has 9 marbles and wins 6 more. 9 + 6: make 10 with 1 from the 6, leaving 5, so 10 + 5 = 15. Write the answer with words: Amal has 15 marbles.
Step 6, Your turn: find 8 + 7 using a bond to 10, and 9 + 3 on a number line. Answer: 8 + 2 = 10, then 5 more gives 15; and 9 hop 3 lands on 12.
Step 1, Take away objects: 12 cubes, remove 5. Cross out five cubes and count the rest: 7 are left. So 12 - 5 = 7. Say it as: twelve take away five leaves seven.
Step 2, Count back on a number line: for 15 - 4 start on 15 and hop back 4: 14, 13, 12, 11. You land on 11, so 15 - 4 = 11. Count the hops, not the start number.
Step 3, Link to adding: since 11 + 4 = 15, then 15 - 4 = 11 must be true. Write the fact family: 4 + 11 = 15, 11 + 4 = 15, 15 - 4 = 11, 15 - 11 = 4. These four go together.
Step 4, Subtract using ten: 14 - 6. Take away 4 to reach 10, then take away the other 2 to get 8. So 14 - 6 = 8. Check by adding: 8 + 6 = 14, which matches the start.
Step 5, Word problem: there are 13 birds on a wall and 7 fly off. Work 13 - 7: 13 - 3 = 10, then 10 - 4 = 6. Answer: 6 birds are left. Check: 6 + 7 = 13.
Step 6, Your turn: solve 16 - 9 and write its fact family. Answer: 16 - 6 = 10, then 10 - 3 = 7, so 16 - 9 = 7. The family is 9 + 7 = 16, 7 + 9 = 16, 16 - 9 = 7, 16 - 7 = 9.

Step 1, Name flat shapes: a clock face is a circle with one curved side and no corners. A book cover is a rectangle with 4 sides and 4 corners. A sandwich cut corner to corner makes a triangle with 3 sides.
Step 2, Count sides and corners: a square has 4 equal sides and 4 corners. A rectangle also has 4 sides, but two are long and two are short. Tap each side and say the count to be sure.
Step 3, Name solid shapes: a ball is a sphere, a tin of beans is a cylinder, a dice is a cube, and a party hat is a cone. Solids can be held and have faces you can feel.
Step 4, Sort by a feature: put a ball, a dice, a tin and a box in two groups, can roll and cannot roll. Ball and tin roll. Dice and box have flat faces only, so they do not roll.
Step 5, Find shapes in a face: a cube has 6 flat faces and every face is a square. Trace around one face of a dice on paper and you draw a square with 4 equal sides.

Step 6, Your turn: name the shape of a coin, a cereal box and a football, and say which of them roll. Answer: circle (flat face of a cylinder), cuboid, sphere. The coin and football roll; the box does not.

Step 1, Compare length: lay a pencil and a crayon with their left ends on the same line. The pencil sticks out further, so the pencil is longer and the crayon is shorter. Starting at the same line is the key.

Step 2, Order three objects: a ribbon, a straw and a toothpick. Line them up from one edge. The order from shortest to longest is toothpick, straw, ribbon. Say: the ribbon is the longest of the three.
Step 3, Measure with cubes: a book is 9 cubes long and a cup is 4 cubes tall. Because 9 is more than 4, the book is longer than the cup is tall. Count with no gaps and no overlaps.
Step 4, Compare weight: hold a bag of rice in one hand and a feather in the other. The rice feels heavier and the feather lighter. A balance tips down on the heavy side, which confirms it.
Step 5, Order by weight: a pumpkin, an apple and a grape. Put them on a balance two at a time. The order from lightest to heaviest is grape, apple, pumpkin. Use words heavier and lighter.
Step 6, Your turn: a rope is 12 cubes long and a stick is 8 cubes long. Which is longer, and by how many cubes? Answer: the rope is longer by 4 cubes, since 12 - 8 = 4.
Step 1, Read o'clock: the short hour hand points to 3 and the long minute hand points to 12. That is 3 o'clock. When the minute hand is on 12, we say o'clock and read only the hour hand.
Step 2, Read half past: the minute hand points to 6 and the hour hand is between 4 and 5. That is half past 4, written 4:30. Half past means the long hand has gone half way round.
Step 3, Show a time: to show half past 7 draw the minute hand on 6. Draw the hour hand halfway between 7 and 8. Check that the long hand points down, since half past always points down.
Step 4, Order the days: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday. Seven days in a week. If today is Tuesday, tomorrow is Wednesday and yesterday was Monday.
Step 5, Day after problem: today is Thursday. Two days later is Saturday, since Friday is one and Saturday is two. Check by counting on the fingers: Friday, Saturday. Answer: Saturday.
Step 6, Your turn: what time is it when the hour hand is on 9 and the minute hand on 12? And what day comes after Friday? Answer: 9 o'clock, and the day after Friday is Saturday.
Step 1, Name the coins: use a coin with the number 1, one with 5 and one with 10. Say the value of each: one, five, ten. Larger number does not always mean bigger coin, so read the number.
Step 2, Make 7 with coins: use one 5 coin and two 1 coins. Count: 5, then 6, 7. So 5 + 1 + 1 = 7. Start with the largest coin and count on with the smaller ones.
Step 3, Make 10 two ways: one 10 coin, or two 5 coins. Both give 10 because 5 + 5 = 10. Different coins can make the same amount, and you can use fewer coins with larger values.
Step 4, Count a handful: a 10 coin, a 5 coin and three 1 coins. Count 10, 15, 16, 17, 18. The total is 18. Counting the biggest first keeps your count quick and correct.
Step 5, Shop problem: a pencil costs 6 and you pay with a 10 coin. Count up from 6 to 10: that is 4 more. So the change is 4. Check: 6 + 4 = 10.
Step 6, Your turn: make 12 using only 5 and 1 coins, then find change from 10 for a sticker costing 3. Answer: two 5 coins and two 1 coins make 12; change is 7 since 3 + 7 = 10.
Step 1, Continue a colour pattern: red, blue, red, blue, red, __. The unit that repeats is red, blue. After red comes blue, so the next one is blue. Read the whole pattern aloud twice.
Step 2, Find the repeating unit: circle, circle, square, circle, circle, square. The unit is circle, circle, square, three shapes long. Next you draw circle, circle, square again to extend it.
Step 3, Number pattern: 2, 4, 6, 8, __. Each number is 2 more than the one before. So the next is 8 + 2 = 10. Say the rule in a sentence: add 2 each time.
Step 4, Make a pattern: use claps and stamps. Clap, clap, stamp, clap, clap, stamp is an AAB pattern. Show it with blocks: yellow, yellow, green, yellow, yellow, green.
Step 5, Sort by one rule: buttons, 5 red and 3 blue. Sort by colour into two groups. Count each group: 5 and 3. There are 2 more red than blue, as 5 - 3 = 2.
Step 6, Your turn: continue star, heart, heart, star, heart, heart, __, __ and sort 4 big and 6 small balls by size. Answer: star, heart; and the groups have 4 big and 6 small, so 2 more small.
Step 1, Break 63 into tens and ones: 6 tens and 3 ones, which is 60 + 3. Draw 6 rods of ten and 3 unit cubes. The 6 in the tens place is worth 60, not 6.
Step 2, Compare 47 and 74: both use digits 4 and 7. Look at the tens first. 7 tens is more than 4 tens, so 74 > 47. Only look at the ones if the tens match.
Step 3, Compare with equal tens: 58 and 52. Tens are both 5, so compare ones: 8 is more than 2. So 58 > 52. Write it as 52 < 58 and read it two ways.
Step 4, Order numbers: 39, 93, 29, 91. Tens: 3, 9, 2, 9. Smallest tens is 29, then 39. The two with 9 tens are compared by ones: 91 before 93. Order is 29, 39, 91, 93.
Step 5, Build a number: with digit cards 5, 8 and 2, make the largest two-digit number using two cards. Put the biggest digit in tens: 85. The smallest is 25. Check, 85 is above 25.
Step 6, Your turn: write 76 as tens and ones, and compare 68 and 86. Answer: 76 is 7 tens and 6 ones, 70 + 6. And 68 < 86 because 6 tens is less than 8 tens.
Step 1, Add without carrying: 34 + 25. Ones: 4 + 5 = 9. Tens: 3 + 2 = 5. So the answer is 59. Line up the ones under ones and tens under tens before adding.
Step 2, Add with carrying: 47 + 28. Ones: 7 + 8 = 15, write 5 and carry 1 ten. Tens: 4 + 2 = 6, plus the carried 1 is 7. The answer is 75.
Step 3, Check with rounding: 47 is about 50 and 28 is about 30, so the sum should be near 80. Our answer 75 is close to 80, so it is sensible. A far-off answer means check again.
Step 4, Word problem: a shop sold 56 mangoes in the morning and 38 in the evening. 56 + 38: ones 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 carry 1; tens 5 + 3 + 1 = 9. Total 94 mangoes.
Step 5, Add by partitioning: 56 + 38 = 56 + 30 + 8 = 86 + 8 = 94. Same answer as the column method, so both agree. Using two methods catches slips in the carry.
Step 6, Your turn: find 68 + 25 and check by rounding. Answer: ones 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 carry 1; tens 6 + 2 + 1 = 9. So 93. Rounded 70 + 30 = 100, near 93.
Step 1, Subtract without borrowing: 79 - 34. Ones: 9 - 4 = 5. Tens: 7 - 3 = 4. The answer is 45. Write the bigger number on top and line up the places.
Step 2, Subtract with borrowing: 52 - 27. Ones: 2 is less than 7, so borrow a ten from the 5. The 5 tens become 4 tens and the 2 ones become 12. Then 12 - 7 = 5 and 4 - 2 = 2. Answer: 25.
Step 3, Check by adding: 25 + 27 = 52, since 5 + 7 = 12, write 2 carry 1, and 2 + 2 + 1 = 5. This matches the number we started with, so 25 is correct.
Step 4, Word problem: a library had 83 books and lent out 46. 83 - 46: borrow, so ones 13 - 6 = 7 and tens 7 - 4 = 3. Answer: 37 books are left.
Step 5, Check with counting up: from 46 to 50 is 4, then 50 to 83 is 33, so 4 + 33 = 37. This second method agrees with 37 and proves the borrowing was done right.
Step 6, Your turn: find 71 - 38 and check by adding. Answer: ones 11 - 8 = 3, tens 6 - 3 = 3, so 33. Check: 33 + 38 = 71.
Step 1, Share equally: 12 sweets among 3 children. Deal one at a time: each child gets 1, then 2, then 3, then 4. Each gets 4 sweets and none are left. So 12 shared by 3 is 4.
Step 2, Group instead: 12 sweets in bags of 3. Circle groups of 3: you can make 4 bags. Sharing 12 into 3 groups and making groups of 3 both give 4.
Step 3, Link to multiplication: 4 bags of 3 sweets is 4 x 3 = 12. Reverse it: 12 divided by 3 = 4. The multiplication fact and the sharing fact are about the same numbers.
Step 4, Check unequal sharing: 10 apples among 3 children gives 3 each with 1 left over, because 3 x 3 = 9. Equal sharing needs the same number for everyone, so one apple remains.
Step 5, Word problem: 20 pencils shared equally among 5 pupils. Count in fives: 5, 10, 15, 20 is four jumps, so each gets 4. Check: 5 x 4 = 20.
Step 6, Your turn: share 18 stickers among 3 friends, and write the multiplication check. Answer: each gets 6, because 3 x 6 = 18.
Step 1, Half of a shape: fold a square paper so the two parts match exactly. Each part is one half, written 1/2. Two halves make a whole, and the parts must be equal in size.
Step 2, Quarters: fold the square again so there are 4 equal parts. Each part is one quarter, 1/4. Colour 1 part and say one quarter is shaded; 3 parts shaded is three quarters.
Step 3, Thirds: a rectangle cut into 3 equal strips gives thirds. Shade 1 strip and write 1/3. If the strips are different sizes then they are not thirds, so measure them.
Step 4, Half of a number: half of 12 cookies means sharing into 2 equal groups, so 12 shared by 2 is 6. A quarter of 12 is 3 cookies since 4 groups of 3 make 12.
Step 5, Spot a wrong split: a circle cut into 2 pieces, one big and one small, is not in halves. Both parts need the same size, so the split fails and is not 1/2.
Step 6, Your turn: what is a quarter of 8 sweets, and how many equal parts make thirds? Answer: a quarter of 8 is 2, since 4 groups of 2 make 8; thirds have 3 equal parts.
Step 1, Measure length: line a ruler's 0 mark with the left end of a pencil. The right end reaches 15, so the pencil is 15 cm long. Always start at 0, not at the edge of the ruler.
Step 2, Choose the tool: use a ruler for a pencil, a tape measure for a desk, and a metre stick for a door. Pick a tool that fits the size, so a ruler for small things.
Step 3, Mass: a bag of sugar on a kitchen scale reads 2 kg. A bag of rice reads 5 kg. The rice is 3 kg heavier since 5 - 2 = 3. Scales measure mass in grams or kilograms.
Step 4, Capacity: a jug holds 1 litre and a cup holds a quarter of a litre. Pouring 4 cups fills the jug, because 4 x 1/4 = 1. Choose litres for large amounts of liquid.
Step 5, Compare lengths: a rope is 90 cm and a stick is 65 cm. The rope is longer by 90 - 65 = 25 cm. Check by adding: 65 + 25 = 90.
Step 6, Your turn: which tool measures a classroom floor, and how much longer is a 120 cm ribbon than an 85 cm one? Answer: a tape measure; 35 cm longer, since 120 - 85 = 35.
Step 1, Read the clock to 5 minutes: the minute hand on 3 means 15 minutes past, because each number is 5 minutes. With the hour hand just past 4, the time is quarter past 4, or 4:15.
Step 2, Count in fives: minute hand on 7 means 7 x 5 = 35 minutes. Count 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. With the hour hand near 6 the time is 6:35, which is 25 minutes to 7.
Step 3, Add money: a pen costs 15 dirhams and a notebook costs 28 dirhams. Add: 5 + 8 = 13, write 3 carry 1; 1 + 2 + 1 = 4. Total is 43 dirhams.
Step 4, Change: pay 50 dirhams for the 43 dirham items. Count up from 43 to 45 is 2, then to 50 is 5, so 7 dirhams change. Check: 43 + 7 = 50.
Step 5, Time later: it is 3:25 and a film starts in 10 minutes. Count on 10 minutes from 25 to get 35. The film starts at 3:35. Check on a clock face: minute hand moves from 5 to 7.
Step 6, Your turn: say the time when the minute hand is on 9 and the hour hand is between 8 and 9, and add 24 + 19 dirhams. Answer: 8:45, quarter to 9; and 24 + 19 = 43 dirhams.
Step 1, Set operations: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} and B = {2, 4, 6}. Union A U B = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, intersection = {2, 4}, difference A - B = {1, 3, 5}. List each element once.
Step 2, Count with the formula n(A U B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A n B) = 5 + 3 - 2 = 6. This agrees with the six elements listed. The formula avoids counting the overlap twice.
Step 3, Survey problem: of 60 students, 35 like tea, 28 like coffee and 10 like both. Either drink: 35 + 28 - 10 = 53. So 60 - 53 = 7 like neither.
Step 4, Function values: f(x) = 2x + 3 on the domain {1, 2, 3} gives f(1) = 5, f(2) = 7, f(3) = 9, so the range is {5, 7, 9}. Each input has exactly one output, so f is a function.
Step 5, Domain: for f(x) = 1/(x - 2), the denominator must not be zero, so the domain is all real numbers except 2. And f(x) = x^2 - 1 gives f(-2) = 4 - 1 = 3.
Step 6, Your turn: if n(A) = 20, n(B) = 15 and n(A U B) = 28, find n(A n B), and find f(4) for f(x) = 3x - 1. Answer: 20 + 15 - 28 = 7; f(4) = 11.
Step 1, Arithmetic progression: a = 5 and d = 3. The 8th term is a + 7d = 5 + 21 = 26. The sum of 8 terms is 8/2 x (5 + 26) = 4 x 31 = 124.
Step 2, Geometric progression: 2, 6, 18, ... has a = 2 and r = 3. The 5th term = 2 x 3^4 = 162. Sum of 5 terms = 2(3^5 - 1)/(3 - 1) = 242. Check: 2 + 6 + 18 + 54 + 162 = 242.
Step 3, Business use: 10,000 invested at 10 percent compound interest grows as a GP with ratio 1.1. After 3 years the amount is 10,000 x 1.1^3 = 13,310.
Step 4, Trigonometry: if tan theta = 3/4 in the first quadrant, the hypotenuse is 5, so sin theta = 3/5 and cos theta = 4/5. Convert degrees to radians with 180 degrees = pi, so 60 degrees = pi/3.
Step 5, Check the GP sum formula with a short case: 3 terms of 2, 6, 18 sum to 2(27 - 1)/2 = 26, and 2 + 6 + 18 = 26. Matching small cases build trust in the formula.
Step 6, Your turn: find the sum of the first 6 terms of the GP 3, 6, 12, ... Answer: S_6 = 3(2^6 - 1)/(2 - 1) = 3 x 63 = 189.
Step 1, Add and multiply complex numbers: (3 + 2i) + (1 - 4i) = 4 - 2i. And (2 + 3i)(1 - i) = 2 - 2i + 3i - 3i^2 = 2 + i + 3 = 5 + i, using i^2 = -1.
Step 2, Conjugate and modulus: the conjugate of 3 - 4i is 3 + 4i. The modulus of 3 - 4i is the root of 9 + 16 = 5. Also (3 - 4i)(3 + 4i) = 9 + 16 = 25, which equals the modulus squared.
Step 3, Quadratic with complex roots: x^2 + 2x + 5 = 0 has discriminant 4 - 20 = -16. So x = (-2 plus or minus 4i)/2 = -1 plus or minus 2i.
Step 4, Check: substitute x = -1 + 2i. x^2 = 1 - 4i + 4i^2 = -3 - 4i. Then x^2 + 2x + 5 = (-3 - 4i) + (-2 + 4i) + 5 = 0. The root works.
Step 5, Real roots: x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0 factorises as (x - 2)(x - 3), giving x = 2 or 3 with discriminant 25 - 24 = 1 > 0. A positive discriminant gives real roots, a negative one gives complex roots.
Step 6, Your turn: find (4 + i)(4 - i) and solve x^2 - 2x + 10 = 0. Answer: 16 + 1 = 17; discriminant 4 - 40 = -36, so x = 1 plus or minus 3i.
Step 1, Factorial and arrangements: 5! = 5 x 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 120. The 5 distinct letters of MATHS can be arranged in 120 ways. For LEVEL, with E twice and L twice, it is 5!/(2! x 2!) = 120/4 = 30.
Step 2, Permutations: P(7, 2) = 7 x 6 = 42 ways to choose a president and a secretary from 7 people, where order matters. Combination: C(8, 3) = 8 x 7 x 6 / 6 = 56 where order does not matter.
Step 3, Committee problem: choose 3 from 5 men and 4 women with 2 men and 1 woman. C(5, 2) x C(4, 1) = 10 x 4 = 40 ways. Multiply the independent choices.
Step 5, Check C(8, 3) = C(8, 5) = 56. Choosing 3 to take is the same as choosing 5 to leave. This symmetry helps with larger numbers, e.g. C(10, 8) = C(10, 2) = 45.
Step 6, Your turn: find C(10, 2) and the number of 4-digit codes from digits 1 to 6 with no repeats. Answer: 45; and P(6, 4) = 6 x 5 x 4 x 3 = 360.
Step 1, Equation of a line: through (1, 2) and (3, 8) the slope is (8 - 2)/(3 - 1) = 3. Using point-slope, y - 2 = 3(x - 1), so y = 3x - 1. Check with (3, 8): 9 - 1 = 8.
Step 2, Parallel and perpendicular: the line 2x + 3y = 6 has slope -2/3. A parallel line has the same slope. A perpendicular line has slope 3/2 because (-2/3) x (3/2) = -1.
Step 3, Intercept form: the line x/4 + y/3 = 1 meets the axes at (4, 0) and (0, 3). Multiply by 12 to get 3x + 4y = 12. Check (4, 0): 12 = 12.
Step 4, Limit by factorising: lim as x approaches 2 of (x^2 - 4)/(x - 2). Direct substitution gives 0/0, so factorise: (x - 2)(x + 2)/(x - 2) = x + 2, which tends to 4.
Step 5, Simple limit: lim as x approaches 3 of (2x + 1) = 7 by substitution. Business use: cost C = 50 + 8x is a line with fixed cost 50 and slope 8 per unit, so 20 units cost 210.
Step 6, Your turn: write the line through (0, -1) with slope 2, and find the limit of (x^2 - 1)/(x - 1) as x approaches 1. Answer: y = 2x - 1; the limit is x + 1 = 2.
Step 1, Mean and deviations: data 4, 8, 6, 10, 12 has mean 40/5 = 8. Deviations are -4, 0, -2, 2, 4. Their squares are 16, 0, 4, 4, 16, which add up to 40.
Step 2, Variance = 40/5 = 8 and standard deviation = root 8 = about 2.83. Check: the deviations are mostly within 3 of the mean, so a spread near 2.83 is believable.
Step 3, Addition rule: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A and B) = 0.2. Then P(A or B) = 0.5 + 0.4 - 0.2 = 0.7. Subtracting the overlap avoids double counting.
Step 4, Two dice: a sum of 7 happens in 6 ways, (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1), out of 36. So P = 6/36 = 1/6.
Step 5, Independent events: if P(A) = 0.6 and P(B) = 0.3 are independent, then P(A and B) = 0.6 x 0.3 = 0.18, and P(A or B) = 0.6 + 0.3 - 0.18 = 0.72.
Step 6, Your turn: find the variance of 2, 4, 6, 8. Answer: mean 5, squared deviations 9, 1, 1, 9 sum to 20, so variance 20/4 = 5.
Step 1, Cartesian product: A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {a, b}. A x B has 3 x 2 = 6 ordered pairs: (1, a), (1, b), (2, a), (2, b), (3, a), (3, b). Order matters, so (1, a) differs from (a, 1).
Step 3, Venn counting: n(A) = 30, n(B) = 25, n(A n B) = 10. So n(A U B) = 30 + 25 - 10 = 45. Only A is 30 - 10 = 20, and only B is 25 - 10 = 15.
Step 4, Domain and range: f(x) = root of (x - 3) needs x - 3 >= 0, so the domain is x >= 3 and the range is y >= 0. For f(x) = x^2 + 1 the range is y >= 1.
Step 5, Power set: for {a, b, c}, the subsets are 2^3 = 8 in number: empty, 3 singletons, 3 pairs and the whole set. A set with n elements has 2^n subsets.
Step 6, Your turn: if n(A) = 4 and n(B) = 5 find n(A x B), and give the domain of 1/(x - 5). Answer: 20; all real numbers except 5.
Step 1, Radians: 150 degrees = 150 x pi/180 = 5 pi/6. And pi/4 radians = 45 degrees. The conversion factor is pi radians = 180 degrees.
Step 2, Identity: if sin x = 3/5 with x in quadrant II, then cos^2 x = 1 - 9/25 = 16/25, so cos x = -4/5 since cosine is negative there. Then tan x = -3/4.
Step 3, Compound angle: sin 75 = sin(45 + 30) = sin 45 cos 30 + cos 45 sin 30 = (root 2/2)(root 3/2) + (root 2/2)(1/2) = (root 6 + root 2)/4, about 0.966.
Step 4, Solve sin x = 1/2 for x in [0, 2 pi]: the principal angle is pi/6, and the second solution is pi - pi/6 = 5 pi/6. Check: sin(5 pi/6) = 1/2.
Step 5, Graphs: y = 2 sin x has amplitude 2 and period 2 pi, with maximum 2 at x = pi/2. y = sin 2x has period pi, so it completes one wave between 0 and pi.
Step 6, Your turn: find cos 2x when cos x = 3/5. Answer: cos 2x = 2 cos^2 x - 1 = 2 x 9/25 - 1 = -7/25.
Step 1, Divide complex numbers: (3 + 4i)/(1 - 2i). Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate 1 + 2i: (3 + 4i)(1 + 2i) / 5 = (3 + 6i + 4i + 8i^2)/5 = (-5 + 10i)/5 = -1 + 2i.
Step 2, Check: (-1 + 2i)(1 - 2i) = -1 + 2i + 2i - 4i^2 = -1 + 4i + 4 = 3 + 4i. This returns the numerator, so the quotient -1 + 2i is correct.
Step 3, Polar form: z = 1 + i has modulus root 2 and argument pi/4, since tan = 1 in the first quadrant. So z = root 2 (cos pi/4 + i sin pi/4). Also |3 - 4i| = 5.
Step 4, Quadratic: x^2 - 2x + 5 = 0 has D = 4 - 20 = -16. So x = (2 plus or minus 4i)/2 = 1 plus or minus 2i. The roots are conjugates, as always with real coefficients.
Step 5, Cube roots of unity: x^2 + x + 1 = 0 gives D = 1 - 4 = -3, so x = (-1 plus or minus i root 3)/2. These are the complex cube roots of 1, and their sum with 1 is 0.
Step 6, Your turn: find (2 + i)^2 and the modulus of 5 + 12i. Answer: 4 + 4i + i^2 = 3 + 4i; modulus is the root of 25 + 144 = 13.
Step 1, Solve 3x - 5 < 7: add 5 to get 3x < 12, so x < 4. On a number line, draw an open circle at 4 and shade left. Test x = 3: 9 - 5 = 4 < 7, true.
Step 2, Double inequality: -3 <= 2x + 1 < 9. Subtract 1: -4 <= 2x < 8. Divide by 2: -2 <= x < 4. So x is in [-2, 4). Test x = 0: 1 lies between -3 and 9.
Step 3, Flip rule: 4 - 3x >= 10 gives -3x >= 6. Dividing by -3 reverses the sign, so x <= -2. Test x = -3: 4 + 9 = 13 >= 10, true.
Step 4, Arrangements: 5 people in a line can be placed in 5! = 120 ways. If 2 specific people must stand together, treat them as one block: 4! x 2! = 24 x 2 = 48 ways.

Step 6, Your turn: convert 3 m 25 cm to cm, and 2 litres 50 ml to ml. Answer: 325 cm, since 300 + 25; and 2050 ml, since 2000 + 50.
Step 1, Continue a number pattern: 5, 10, 15, 20, __. Each term is 5 more than the one before. The next two are 25 and 30. Describe it as: start at 5 and add 5 each time.
Step 2, Decreasing pattern: 90, 80, 70, 60. The rule is subtract 10 each time. Continuing gives 50, 40. Check using the gap: 90 - 80 = 10, 80 - 70 = 10, so the rule is steady.
Step 3, Find the missing term: 4, 7, __, 13, 16. The gap is 3 each time (7 - 4 = 3, 16 - 13 = 3). The missing term is 7 + 3 = 10, and 10 + 3 = 13 confirms it.
Step 4, Shape pattern: triangle, square, square, triangle, square, square. The repeating unit is triangle, square, square, so the 7th shape is a triangle and the 9th is a square.
Step 5, Growing pattern with matchsticks: 1 square uses 4 sticks, 2 squares in a row use 7, 3 squares use 10. Each new square adds 3 sticks. So 4 squares use 13 sticks.
Step 6, Your turn: continue 3, 6, 9, 12 and find the 5th and 6th terms of 2, 5, 8, 11. Answer: next terms 15, 18; and the sequence adds 3, so 14 and 17.
Step 1, Write money: 2 dirhams 50 fils is written 2.50 dirhams. 100 fils = 1 dirham, so 250 fils = 2.50 dirhams. Always write two digits after the point.
Step 2, Add: a pen costs 3.75 and an eraser costs 1.50. Fils: 75 + 50 = 125, so write 25 and carry 1 dirham. Dirhams: 3 + 1 + 1 = 5. Total 5.25 dirhams.
Step 3, Subtract: you have 10.00 dirhams and spend 6.35. 10.00 - 6.35: change 3.65 because 6.35 + 3.65 = 10.00 (35 + 65 = 100 fils, 6 + 3 + 1 = 10).
Step 4, Give change by counting up: item costs 7.60, you pay 10.00. From 7.60 to 8.00 is 40 fils, then to 10.00 is 2 dirhams. Change is 2.40 dirhams.
Step 5, Multiply: 4 notebooks at 2.25 each. 4 x 2 = 8 dirhams, 4 x 25 fils = 100 fils = 1 dirham. Total 9.00 dirhams. Check with rounding, 4 x 2.25 is near 4 x 2 = 8.
Step 6, Your turn: find 4.80 + 2.45 and the change from 10.00 after buying a 7.30 snack. Answer: 7.25 dirhams; change is 2.70, since 7.30 + 2.70 = 10.00.
Step 1, Tally chart: favourite fruits of 20 pupils. Mark each vote with a stroke and bundle the fifth. Apples ||||, bananas |||| ||, mangoes |||. Counts are 4, 7 and 3.
Step 2, Check the total: 4 + 7 + 3 = 14, but we expect 20 pupils. So 6 more votes went to grapes. Adding the totals shows a missing group, a quick check for every tally chart.
Step 3, Pictograph: let each picture mean 2 pupils. Bananas have 7 votes, which is 3 pictures and a half picture. Half a picture means 1 pupil. So 3 x 2 + 1 = 7.
Step 4, Bar graph: scale the vertical axis 0 to 8 in steps of 1. Draw a bar to 4 for apples, 7 for bananas, 3 for mangoes, 6 for grapes. Give the graph a title and label both axes.
Step 5, Read the graph: bananas are the most popular and mangoes the least. The difference is 7 - 3 = 4 pupils. Total pupils are 4 + 7 + 3 + 6 = 20, which agrees.
Step 6, Your turn: using bars of 5, 9 and 2, how many more is the tallest than the shortest, and what is the total? Answer: 9 - 2 = 7 more, and the total is 5 + 9 + 2 = 16.
Step 1, Read 7,308: seven thousand, three hundred and eight. Place values: 7 thousands, 3 hundreds, 0 tens, 8 ones. The zero holds the tens place. Expanded: 7000 + 300 + 0 + 8.
Step 2, Write from words: four thousand, six hundred and fifty is 4,650. Put 4 in thousands, 6 in hundreds, 5 in tens and 0 in ones. Check by reading 4,650 back in words.
Step 3, Compare 5,962 and 5,926: thousands equal (5), hundreds equal (9), tens 6 is greater than 2. So 5,962 > 5,926. Compare place by place from the left.
Step 4, Round 6,478 to the nearest hundred: look at the tens digit 7. It is 5 or more, so round up to 6,500. To the nearest thousand look at hundreds digit 4: round down to 6,000.
Step 6, Your turn: round 8,251 to the nearest hundred and nearest thousand, and write 9,070 in words. Answer: 8,300 and 8,000; nine thousand and seventy.
Step 1, Add 4,256 + 3,789 in columns. Ones: 6 + 9 = 15, write 5 carry 1. Tens: 5 + 8 + 1 = 14, write 4 carry 1. Hundreds: 2 + 7 + 1 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Thousands: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. Sum 8,045.

Step 2, Estimate: 4,300 + 3,800 = 8,100, near 8,045. Reasonable. Subtract 7,003 - 2,846: borrow through the zeros. Ones 13 - 6 = 7, tens 9 - 4 = 5, hundreds 9 - 8 = 1, thousands 6 - 2 = 4. Answer 4,157.
Step 3, Check subtraction by adding: 4,157 + 2,846 = 7,003 (7 + 6 = 13, 5 + 4 + 1 = 10, 1 + 8 + 1 = 10, 4 + 2 + 1 = 7). The sum matches, so 4,157 is correct.
Step 4, Multi-step problem: a shop has 5,200 items. It sells 1,845 on Monday and receives 2,300 on Tuesday. After Monday: 5,200 - 1,845 = 3,355. After Tuesday: 3,355 + 2,300 = 5,655 items.
Step 5, Check with estimation: 5,200 - 1,800 = 3,400, then + 2,300 = 5,700. This is close to 5,655, so the working is sensible. Write each step as its own line.
Step 6, Your turn: a school had 6,400 books, gave away 2,175 and bought 1,850. How many now? Answer: 6,400 - 2,175 = 4,225; then 4,225 + 1,850 = 6,075 books.
Step 1, Divide 756 by 3 using short division. 7 hundreds / 3 = 2 with 1 left. That 1 hundred joins 5 tens to make 15 tens; 15 / 3 = 5. Then 6 / 3 = 2. Answer 252.
Step 2, Check by multiplying: 252 x 3 = 756 (2 x 3 = 6, 5 x 3 = 15 write 5 carry 1, 2 x 3 + 1 = 7). The product equals the dividend, so 252 is right.
Step 3, Division with remainder: 1,475 / 6. 14 / 6 = 2 rem 2; 27 / 6 = 4 rem 3; 35 / 6 = 5 rem 5. So 245 remainder 5. Check: 245 x 6 = 1,470, plus 5 gives 1,475.
Step 4, Four digits: 3,648 / 4. 36 / 4 = 9; 4 / 4 = 1; 8 / 4 = 2. But 3 / 4 gives 0 first, so the quotient starts at 36: result 912. Check: 912 x 4 = 3,648.
Step 5, Word problem: 1,284 oranges are packed in boxes of 6. 12 / 6 = 2; 8 / 6 = 1 rem 2; 24 / 6 = 4. So 214 boxes with nothing left. Check: 214 x 6 = 1,284.
Step 6, Your turn: divide 2,596 by 4 and 905 by 5. Answer: 2,596 / 4 = 649 since 649 x 4 = 2,596; and 905 / 5 = 181 since 181 x 5 = 905.
Step 1, Factors of 24: test numbers in pairs. 1 x 24, 2 x 12, 3 x 8, 4 x 6. Factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. A factor divides the number exactly.
Step 2, Multiples: the multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36. Multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24, 32, 40. Multiples come from counting by the number, while factors go into it.
Step 3, Common multiples of 6 and 8: both lists contain 24, and the next common multiple is 48. The lowest common multiple (LCM) is 24. Write the first match you find.
Step 4, Common factors of 12 and 18: factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12; factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 6. Greatest is 6.
Step 5, Word problem: two buses leave a stop, one every 6 minutes and one every 8 minutes. They leave together at 9:00. They next leave together after 24 minutes, at 9:24.
Step 6, Your turn: list the common factors of 20 and 30, and the LCM of 4 and 10. Answer: common factors are 1, 2, 5, 10; LCM of 4 and 10 is 20.
Step 1, Compare 3/5 and 4/5: same denominator, so compare numerators. 4 > 3, so 4/5 > 3/5. For unlike denominators, 1/2 is greater than 1/4 because halves are bigger parts.
Step 2, Add: 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8 since the denominators match. Subtract: 7/10 - 3/10 = 4/10, which simplifies to 2/5 (divide top and bottom by 2).
Step 3, Tenths to decimals: 3/10 = 0.3 because one tenth is 0.1. So 7/10 = 0.7. Hundredths: 45/100 = 0.45, with 4 tenths and 5 hundredths.
Step 4, Compare decimals: 0.6 and 0.45. Write 0.6 as 0.60. Now compare hundredths: 60 > 45, so 0.6 > 0.45. A longer decimal is not always bigger.
Step 5, Money link: 0.75 dirham is 75 fils, which is 75/100 = 3/4 of a dirham. Check: 3/4 of 100 fils = 75 fils. Fractions, decimals and money agree.
Step 6, Your turn: find 5/9 - 2/9 and write 3/100 and 6/10 as decimals. Answer: 3/9 = 1/3; and 0.03 and 0.6.
Step 1, Perimeter of a rectangle 9 cm by 5 cm: add all four sides, 9 + 5 + 9 + 5 = 28 cm. Or use 2 x (9 + 5) = 2 x 14 = 28 cm. Perimeter is the distance around.
Step 2, Area of the same rectangle: length x width = 9 x 5 = 45 square cm. Area counts squares inside, so the unit is square cm (cm2), not cm.
Step 3, Find a missing side: a rectangle has perimeter 30 cm and length 10 cm. Half the perimeter is 15, and 15 - 10 = 5. So the width is 5 cm and area is 10 x 5 = 50 cm2.
Step 4, Convert units: 2.5 m = 250 cm since 1 m = 100 cm. A ribbon 3 m 40 cm long is 340 cm. For mass, 3 kg 200 g = 3,200 g, and 4,500 ml = 4 l 500 ml.
Step 5, Word problem: a garden is 12 m by 8 m. Fencing is its perimeter: 2 x (12 + 8) = 40 m. Grass area is 12 x 8 = 96 m2. Fence length and grass area use different units.
Step 6, Your turn: find the perimeter and area of a 15 m by 6 m field. Answer: perimeter 2 x 21 = 42 m; area 15 x 6 = 90 m2.
Step 1, Read a timetable: bus leaves School at 7:45 a.m. and arrives at Market at 8:20 a.m. From 7:45 to 8:00 is 15 minutes, then 20 more. Journey time 35 minutes.
Step 2, 24-hour time: 3:15 p.m. is 15:15, found by adding 12 to 3. And 18:40 is 6:40 p.m. by subtracting 12. Midnight is 00:00, noon is 12:00.
Step 3, Calendar: October has 31 days, and if 5 October is a Monday then 12 and 19 are Mondays too. So 26 October is also a Monday, and 31 October is 5 days later, a Saturday.
Step 4, Days between: from 12 March to 4 April. Days left in March are 31 - 12 = 19, plus 4 days of April gives 23 days. Always count the month length you cross.
Step 5, Combine time: a film runs 1 hour 45 minutes and begins at 6:30 p.m. Add 1 hour to get 7:30, then 45 minutes to get 8:15 p.m. Check: 7:30 + 30 = 8:00, 15 more = 8:15.
Step 6, Your turn: a train leaves at 10:50 and arrives at 13:05. How long is the journey? Answer: 10 minutes to 11:00, then 2 hours to 13:00, plus 5 minutes; total 2 hours 15 minutes.
Step 1, Read a bar graph: bars show pupils per sport. Football 12, cricket 9, tennis 5, swimming 9. The scale is 2 per square, so read the top of each bar against the axis.
Step 2, Find the mode: the value that occurs most often. In 12, 9, 5, 9 the number 9 appears twice, so the mode is 9. In the graph, cricket and swimming share it.
Step 3, Line graph: temperatures at 6, 8, 10, 12 o'clock were 18, 21, 26, 29 degrees. The line rises each time. From 8 to 10 the rise is 26 - 21 = 5 degrees.
Step 4, Find the greatest rise: between 6 and 8 the rise is 3, 8 to 10 is 5, 10 to 12 is 3. The steepest part of the line is 8 to 10, with a rise of 5.

Step 6, Your turn: find the mode of 4, 7, 7, 3, 7, 4 and the rise from 21 to 29 degrees. Answer: mode is 7, which appears three times; rise is 8 degrees.
Step 1, Number pattern: 7, 14, 21, 28, __. The rule is add 7, so the next terms are 35 and 42. These are the multiples of 7. Check: 6 x 7 = 42.
Step 2, Pattern with a changing step: 2, 3, 5, 8, 12. Differences are 1, 2, 3, 4, so the next difference is 5 and the next term is 17. Always check the gaps.
Step 3, Money problem: three books cost 12.50, 8.75 and 15.25 dirhams. Total: 12.50 + 8.75 = 21.25, plus 15.25 = 36.50 dirhams. Align the decimal points in columns.
Step 4, Change: pay with 50 dirhams. 50.00 - 36.50 = 13.50. Check by counting up: 36.50 to 37 is 0.50, to 50 is 13, so 13.50. Change is 13.50 dirhams.
Step 5, Unit price: 4 pens cost 14 dirhams, so one pen costs 14 / 4 = 3.50 dirhams. Then 9 pens cost 9 x 3.50 = 31.50 dirhams. Check: 9 x 3 = 27 and 9 x 0.50 = 4.50, total 31.50.

Step 1, Read 4,52,368 in the lakh system: four lakh fifty-two thousand three hundred sixty-eight. Commas split it as lakhs, thousands, then hundreds. The same number in the million system is written 452,368.
Step 2, Link lakh to million: 10 lakh = 1,000,000 = 1 million. So 25,00,000 is 25 lakh, which is 2,500,000 or two and a half million. Divide a lakh count by 10 to get millions.
Step 3, Compare 7,35,420 and 7,53,240: both have 7 lakh. Next compare ten-thousands: 3 against 5. Since 5 > 3, the second number is bigger, so 7,35,420 < 7,53,240.
Step 4, Round 6,48,572 to the nearest thousand: look at the hundreds digit 5, so round up to 6,49,000. To the nearest lakh, the remainder 48,572 is less than 50,000, so round down to 6,00,000.
Step 5, Write from words: nine lakh seven thousand and forty is 9,07,040. The empty ten-thousands place holds a 0 and the hundreds place holds 0. Reading 9,07,040 aloud checks it.

Step 6, Your turn: round 5,67,891 to the nearest ten thousand and write it in words. Answer: 5,70,000, since the thousands digit 7 rounds up; the original reads five lakh sixty-seven thousand eight hundred ninety-one.
Step 1, Problem: a shop buys 24 boxes of 35 pens, sells 650 pens, and packs the rest in packs of 5. First multiply: 24 x 35 = 24 x 30 + 24 x 5 = 720 + 120 = 840 pens.
Step 2, Subtract the sales: 840 - 650 = 190 pens remain. Then divide into packs of 5: 190 / 5 = 38. So 38 packs can be made, and nothing is left over because 38 x 5 = 190.
Step 3, Check by working backwards: 38 x 5 = 190, 190 + 650 = 840, and 840 / 24 = 35. Each reverse step returns to the number before, so the chain is correct.
Step 4, Order of operations: 5 + 3 x 4 means multiply first, so 3 x 4 = 12 and 5 + 12 = 17, not 32. With brackets, (5 + 3) x 4 = 32. Brackets change the order.
Step 5, Another multi-step problem: 6,250 - (3 x 1,200 + 475). Brackets first: 3 x 1,200 = 3,600, plus 475 = 4,075. Then 6,250 - 4,075 = 2,175.
Step 6, Your turn: 18 boxes of 25 pencils are bought, 130 are given away, the rest are shared among 4 classes. Answer: 18 x 25 = 450; 450 - 130 = 320; 320 / 4 = 80 each.
Step 2, Prime factors: 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 and 48 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3. HCF takes shared primes with the smaller powers, 2 x 2 x 3 = 12. LCM takes the larger powers, 2^4 x 3^2 = 144.
Step 3, Check with the product rule: HCF x LCM = product of the numbers. 12 x 144 = 1,728 and 36 x 48 = 1,728. They match, so both answers are right.
Step 4, HCF word problem: ribbons of 36 cm and 48 cm are cut into equal pieces with no waste. The longest piece is the HCF, 12 cm. That gives 3 + 4 = 7 pieces in all.
Step 5, LCM word problem: two bells ring every 12 and every 18 minutes. Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36. Multiples of 18: 18, 36. They ring together again after 36 minutes, which is the LCM.
Step 6, Your turn: find the HCF and LCM of 24 and 40. Answer: HCF is 8 (24 = 8 x 3, 40 = 8 x 5) and LCM is 24 x 40 / 8 = 120.
Step 1, Add unlike fractions: 2/3 + 3/4. The common denominator is 12. 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12. Sum = 17/12, which is the mixed number 1 5/12.
Step 2, Subtract mixed numbers: 3 1/2 - 1 3/4. Convert to improper fractions: 7/2 and 7/4. Use denominator 4: 14/4 - 7/4 = 7/4 = 1 3/4. Check: 1 3/4 + 1 3/4 = 3 2/4 = 3 1/2.
Step 3, Multiply fractions: 2/5 x 3/4 = (2 x 3) / (5 x 4) = 6/20. Simplify by dividing top and bottom by 2 to get 3/10. Cancel first when you can: 2 and 4 share a factor 2.
Step 4, Multiply mixed numbers: 1 1/2 x 2 2/3. Change to 3/2 x 8/3. The 3s cancel, leaving 8/2 = 4. Check by estimating: 1.5 x 2.7 is about 4.
Step 5, Word problem: a tank is 3/4 full and 2/5 of the water is used. Used = 2/5 x 3/4 = 6/20 = 3/10 of the tank. Left = 3/4 - 3/10 = 15/20 - 6/20 = 9/20.
Step 6, Your turn: find 5/6 - 1/4 and 2 1/4 x 4/9. Answer: 10/12 - 3/12 = 7/12; and 9/4 x 4/9 = 1.
Step 1, Add decimals: 12.45 + 3.8. Write 3.8 as 3.80 and line up the decimal points. 12.45 + 3.80 = 16.25. Keeping points aligned stops place-value mistakes.
Step 2, Subtract: 10 - 6.37. Write 10 as 10.00. Then 10.00 - 6.37 = 3.63. Check by adding: 3.63 + 6.37 = 10.00, which returns the start.
Step 3, Multiply: 2.5 x 1.2. Ignore the points: 25 x 12 = 300. The two numbers have 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places, so the answer is 3.00 = 3. Estimate: 2.5 x 1 is 2.5, and a bit more is 3.
Step 4, Money problem: rice costs 24.60 per kg and you buy 3.5 kg. 24.6 x 3 = 73.8 and 24.6 x 0.5 = 12.3. Total 86.1, so you pay 86.10.
Step 5, Measures link: 2.75 m = 275 cm because 1 m = 100 cm. 0.6 kg = 600 g. A rope of 4.5 m cut into pieces of 0.75 m gives 4.5 / 0.75 = 6 pieces, since 0.75 x 6 = 4.5.
Step 6, Your turn: find 7.25 + 4.9 and 1.5 x 0.8. Answer: 7.25 + 4.90 = 12.15; and 15 x 8 = 120 with two decimal places gives 1.20 = 1.2.
Step 1, Area of a rectangle 14 cm by 9 cm: length x width = 14 x 9 = 126 cm2. Perimeter is a different quantity: 2 x (14 + 9) = 46 cm. Area uses square units.
Step 2, Area of a triangle with base 12 cm and height 7 cm: half x base x height = 1/2 x 12 x 7 = 6 x 7 = 42 cm2. The height must be at right angles to the base.
Step 3, Check the triangle: it is half of a 12 by 7 rectangle. That rectangle has area 84 cm2 and half of 84 is 42 cm2, which agrees.
Step 4, Volume of a cuboid 8 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm: length x width x height = 8 x 5 x 4 = 160 cm3. Check: bottom layer has 8 x 5 = 40 cubes, 4 layers give 160.
Step 5, Capacity link: a tank 50 cm by 40 cm by 30 cm has volume 50 x 40 x 30 = 60,000 cm3. Since 1,000 cm3 = 1 litre, the tank holds 60 litres.
Step 6, Your turn: find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 9 cm, and the volume of a 6 by 5 by 3 cm cuboid. Answer: 1/2 x 10 x 9 = 45 cm2; 6 x 5 x 3 = 90 cm3.
Step 1, Classify angles: 65 degrees is acute (less than 90), 90 is a right angle, 130 is obtuse (between 90 and 180), 180 is a straight angle, and 250 is reflex (more than 180).

Step 2, Measure with a protractor: place its centre on the vertex and its zero line along one arm. Read the scale that starts at 0 on that arm. If the angle opens like a corner narrower than a square, read the smaller number, e.g. 65.

Step 3, Draw 110 degrees: draw a base line, mark the vertex, centre the protractor and zero on the base. Mark a dot at 110 on the scale, remove the protractor and join the vertex to the dot. It is obtuse.
Step 4, Find a missing angle: a triangle has angles 50 and 70. The angles of a triangle add up to 180, so the third angle is 180 - 50 - 70 = 60 degrees. In a quadrilateral they total 360.

Step 5, Classify polygons: pentagon 5 sides, hexagon 6 sides, octagon 8 sides. A regular polygon has equal sides and equal angles. A quadrilateral with angles 90, 80, 100 has fourth angle 360 - 270 = 90.
Step 6, Your turn: find the third angle of a triangle with angles 35 and 85, and name a polygon with 8 sides. Answer: 180 - 120 = 60 degrees; an octagon.
Step 1, Mean: quiz scores 12, 15, 9, 15, 14. Add them: 12 + 15 + 9 + 15 + 14 = 65. Divide by the 5 scores: 65 / 5 = 13. The mean is 13.
Step 2, Median: order the scores 9, 12, 14, 15, 15. The middle one is 14. For an even count, 8, 10, 12, 20, take the two middle values: (10 + 12) / 2 = 11.
Step 3, Mode: in 9, 12, 14, 15, 15 the value 15 appears twice, more than any other. So the mode is 15. A set can have more than one mode or none at all.
Step 4, Read a line graph: rainfall for Jan to Apr is 20, 35, 50, 40 mm. The line goes up then down. The highest point is 50 in March, and the fall from March to April is 10 mm.
Step 5, Use the mean: the mean of 4 months of rainfall is (20 + 35 + 50 + 40) / 4 = 145 / 4 = 36.25 mm. Check: 36.25 is between the lowest 20 and the highest 50.
Step 6, Your turn: find the mean, median and mode of 6, 8, 8, 10, 13. Answer: sum 45, mean 9; median 8 (middle of five); mode 8.
Step 1, Use a letter: a pencil costs x dirhams, so 5 pencils cost 5x. If a pencil costs 3, 5x = 15. The letter stands for a number we may not know yet.
Step 2, Solve x + 7 = 15. To undo adding 7, subtract 7 from both sides: x = 15 - 7 = 8. Check: 8 + 7 = 15, which is true.
Step 3, Solve 3n = 21. To undo multiplying by 3, divide both sides by 3: n = 7. Check: 3 x 7 = 21. Do the same operation on both sides to keep the equation balanced.
Step 4, Two-step equation: 2y + 3 = 17. Subtract 3 first: 2y = 14. Then divide by 2: y = 7. Check: 2 x 7 + 3 = 14 + 3 = 17. Correct.
Step 5, Word problem: a number plus 12 is 30. Write n + 12 = 30, so n = 30 - 12 = 18. Check: 18 + 12 = 30. Always test the answer in the original sentence.
Step 6, Your turn: solve 3x - 4 = 11. Answer: add 4 to both sides to get 3x = 15, then divide by 3 so x = 5. Check: 3 x 5 - 4 = 11.
Step 1, Read in the Indian system: 3,45,67,890 is three crore forty-five lakh sixty-seven thousand eight hundred ninety. In the international system the same number is 34,567,890.
Step 2, Estimate a sum: 4,897 + 3,112. Round each to the nearest thousand: 5,000 + 3,000 = 8,000. The exact sum is 8,009, very close to the estimate, so it is sensible.
Step 3, Roman numerals: XLIV = XL + IV = 40 + 4 = 44. And 1,994 = 1000 + 900 + 90 + 4 = M + CM + XC + IV = MCMXCIV. A smaller symbol before a larger one is subtracted.
Step 4, Roman rules: V, L and D are never repeated, and I, X, C, M repeat at most 3 times. So 4 is IV, not IIII, and 9 is IX. Check XIX = 10 + 9 = 19.

Step 5, Round to compare: a city has 4,86,215 people and another 5,12,780. Rounded to the nearest lakh these are 5,00,000 and 5,00,000, so round to the nearest ten thousand: 4,90,000 and 5,10,000. The second is larger by about 20,000.

Step 1, Use properties: 25 x 48. Write 48 as 50 - 2 and use the distributive property: 25 x 50 - 25 x 2 = 1,250 - 50 = 1,200. Check: 25 x 48 is 25 x 4 x 12 = 100 x 12 = 1,200.
Step 2, Divisibility tests on 3,726: digit sum 3 + 7 + 2 + 6 = 18, which is a multiple of 9, so 3,726 is divisible by 3 and 9. It ends in 6, so it is divisible by 2, and so by 6.
Step 3, Check 4: the last two digits 26 are not divisible by 4, so 3,726 is not divisible by 4. Verify: 3,726 / 6 = 621 exactly, since 6 x 621 = 3,726.
Step 4, Prime factors of 84: 84 = 2 x 42 = 2 x 2 x 21 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 7. For 70: 2 x 5 x 7. Both share 2 and 7, so HCF(84, 70) = 14.
Step 5, LCM of 42 and 70: 42 = 2 x 3 x 7 and 70 = 2 x 5 x 7. Take each prime once with the highest power: 2 x 3 x 5 x 7 = 210. Check: HCF 14 x LCM 210 = 2,940 = 42 x 70.
Step 6, Your turn: test 1,512 for 9 and 4, and find the HCF and LCM of 18 and 24. Answer: digit sum 9 so divisible by 9; 12 is divisible by 4 so yes; HCF 6, LCM 72.
Step 1, Compare 3/4 and 5/6. The common denominator is 12: 3/4 = 9/12 and 5/6 = 10/12. Since 10 > 9, 5/6 is the larger fraction.
Step 3, Convert to a decimal: 3/8 means 3 divided by 8 = 0.375, since 8 x 0.375 = 3. So 3/8 = 0.375. Also 7/20 = 35/100 = 0.35.
Step 4, Add decimals: 6.75 + 2.8 = 6.75 + 2.80 = 9.55. Subtract: 5 - 2.36 = 5.00 - 2.36 = 2.64. Align decimal points, and add zeros to make the same number of places.
Step 5, Word problem: Sara runs 2.4 km and walks 3/4 km. Change 3/4 to 0.75. Total = 2.4 + 0.75 = 3.15 km. Check with fractions: 2 2/5 + 3/4 = 2 8/20 + 15/20 = 3 3/20 = 3.15.
Step 1, Locate on a number line: -3 is 3 steps left of 0. Moving right is positive, left is negative. So -3 + 7 means start at -3 and move 7 right, landing on 4.
Step 2, Subtract: 5 - 9. Start at 5 and move 9 left, passing 0. That is 5 steps to 0 and 4 more, so 5 - 9 = -4. Check: -4 + 9 = 5.
Step 3, Two negatives: -6 - 2 means start at -6 and move 2 more left, giving -8. The number gets smaller, so -8 < -6.
Step 4, Subtracting a negative: -4 - (-7) = -4 + 7 = 3. Taking away a negative acts like adding the positive. Check with the number line: from -4 move 7 right to land on 3.
Step 5, Temperature problem: morning temperature is -5 degrees and noon is 8 degrees. Rise = 8 - (-5) = 8 + 5 = 13 degrees. On a thermometer, count 5 up to 0 and 8 more, total 13.
Step 6, Your turn: find -8 + 3 and 6 - (-4). Answer: -8 + 3 = -5 (move 3 right from -8), and 6 - (-4) = 6 + 4 = 10.
Step 1, Rectangle 12 cm by 7 cm: perimeter = 2 x (12 + 7) = 38 cm. Area = 12 x 7 = 84 cm2. Perimeter is a length in cm and area is in square cm.
Step 2, Square of side 9 cm: perimeter = 4 x 9 = 36 cm. Area = 9 x 9 = 81 cm2. Reverse it: a square with perimeter 40 cm has side 40 / 4 = 10 cm and area 100 cm2.
Step 3, Composite shape: an L-shape is a 10 cm by 6 cm rectangle with a 4 cm by 3 cm corner removed. Area = 10 x 6 - 4 x 3 = 60 - 12 = 48 cm2.
Step 4, Perimeter of the L-shape: a corner notch does not change the perimeter, since the outer boundary is shifted but the same total length. So perimeter = 2 x (10 + 6) = 32 cm.
Step 5, Word problem: a 20 m by 13 m plot needs fencing and turf. Fence = perimeter = 2 x (20 + 13) = 66 m. Turf = area = 20 x 13 = 260 m2. Different units for different questions.
Step 6, Your turn: find the perimeter and area of a rectangle 25 m by 16 m. Answer: perimeter 2 x 41 = 82 m; area 25 x 16 = 400 m2.
Step 1, Write expressions: a pencil costs p dirhams. Five pencils cost 5p. Ali has k stickers and gets 7 more: k + 7. A square of side s has perimeter 4s.
Step 2, Evaluate: if p = 3, then 5p = 15. If k = 12, then k + 7 = 19. Replace the letter with the number and then calculate.
Step 3, Solve x + 9 = 20. Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 20 - 9 = 11. Check: 11 + 9 = 20, so the equation balances.
Step 4, Solve 3n = 27. Divide both sides by 3: n = 9. Square problem: perimeter 36 cm, so 4s = 36 and s = 36 / 4 = 9 cm. Check: 4 x 9 = 36.
Step 5, Word problem: I think of a number, double it and add 5, and get 19. So 2x + 5 = 19. Subtract 5: 2x = 14, then divide by 2: x = 7.
Step 6, Your turn: write an expression for 3 notebooks at n each plus a pen costing 4, and solve 2x + 5 = 19 by checking 7. Answer: 3n + 4; and 2 x 7 + 5 = 19, so x = 7.
Step 1, Draw a bar graph: marks of 5 students are 14, 18, 12, 16, 20. Choose the scale 0 to 20 in steps of 2, draw equal-width bars with gaps, and label both axes and the title.
Step 2, Find the mean: add 14 + 18 + 12 + 16 + 20 = 80, then divide by 5. The mean is 16. Check that 16 lies between the lowest 12 and the highest 20.
Step 3, Read from the graph: the highest bar is 20 and the lowest is 12, so the range is 20 - 12 = 8. Four of the five students scored 14 or above, since only 12 is below 14.
Step 4, Lines of symmetry: a rectangle has 2 (one vertical, one horizontal), a square has 4, an equilateral triangle has 3, and a circle has infinitely many. The letter A has 1 vertical line.

Step 5, Test a line: fold a paper rectangle along its diagonal and the corners do not match, so a diagonal is not a line of symmetry for a rectangle. Only the lines through midpoints of opposite sides work.
Step 6, Your turn: find the mean of 7, 9, 12, 8, 14 and the lines of symmetry of a regular pentagon. Answer: sum 50, mean 10; and a regular pentagon has 5 lines of symmetry.

Step 1, Multiply with signs: (-6) x 4. A positive times a negative is negative, so the answer is -24. Think of it as 4 jumps of 6 to the left. Then (-5) x (-3) = 15, since two negatives give a positive.
Step 2, Divide with signs: -36 / 9 = -4, because 9 x (-4) = -36. And -48 / (-6) = 8, because (-6) x 8 = -48. Same signs give a positive quotient, different signs give a negative.
Step 3, Check the distributive property: (-4) x (7 + 3) = (-4) x 10 = -40. Also (-4) x 7 + (-4) x 3 = -28 + (-12) = -40. Both sides agree, which confirms the property.
Step 4, Word problem: the temperature drops 3 degrees every hour for 5 hours, starting at 2 degrees. Change = 5 x (-3) = -15. Final = 2 + (-15) = -13 degrees.
Step 5, Mixed expression: (-3) x 4 + 10 / (-2). Multiply and divide first: -12 and -5. Then add: -12 + (-5) = -17. Check by estimating signs: both parts are negative so the sum is negative.
Step 1, Multiply fractions: 3/4 x 2/5 = 6/20 = 3/10 after dividing top and bottom by 2. Cancelling first also works: 2 and 4 share a factor of 2, leaving 3/2 x 1/5 = 3/10.
Step 2, Divide fractions: 2/3 divided by 4/5 means 2/3 x 5/4, the reciprocal flipped. That is 10/12 = 5/6. Check: 5/6 x 4/5 = 20/30 = 2/3, which is the start.
Step 3, Mixed numbers: 2 1/2 divided by 5/6. Write 5/2 x 6/5. The 5s cancel and 6/2 = 3, so the answer is 3. Estimate: 2.5 / 0.83 is about 3.
Step 4, Multiply decimals: 3.6 x 0.25. Do 36 x 25 = 900 and count 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places, so 0.900 = 0.9. Divide: 7.2 / 0.8 = 72 / 8 = 9 after shifting the points one place.
Step 5, Word problem: 12.6 kg of rice is packed in 0.9 kg bags. 12.6 / 0.9 = 126 / 9 = 14 bags. Check: 14 x 0.9 = 12.6, so no rice is left over.
Step 6, Your turn: find 3/5 divided by 9/10 and 6.3 divided by 0.7. Answer: 3/5 x 10/9 = 30/45 = 2/3; and 63 / 7 = 9.
Step 1, Mean: 8 students scored 12, 7, 9, 12, 15, 10, 12, 11. Sum = 88, and 88 / 8 = 11. The mean is 11. Pair check: 19 + 21 + 25 + 23 = 88.
Step 2, Median: sort to 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 12, 12, 15. With 8 values the median is the average of the 4th and 5th: (11 + 12) / 2 = 11.5.
Step 3, Mode and range: 12 appears three times, more than any other value, so the mode is 12. The range is highest minus lowest = 15 - 7 = 8.
Step 4, Read a bar graph: bars of height 6, 9, 4 and 11 show books read in four weeks. Total = 30, mean = 7.5, and the biggest difference between weeks is 11 - 4 = 7.
Step 5, Compare averages: mean 11 and median 11.5 are close, so the data has no big outliers. If one score were 40, the mean would jump while the median barely moves.
Step 6, Your turn: find mean, median, mode and range of 4, 9, 6, 9, 12. Answer: mean 40 / 5 = 8; median 9 (sorted 4, 6, 9, 9, 12); mode 9; range 12 - 4 = 8.
Step 1, Solve 3x + 5 = 20. Subtract 5 from both sides: 3x = 15. Divide both sides by 3: x = 5. Check: 3 x 5 + 5 = 20, so the equation balances.
Step 2, Solve x/4 - 2 = 3. Add 2 to both sides: x/4 = 5. Multiply both sides by 4: x = 20. Check: 20 / 4 - 2 = 5 - 2 = 3.
Step 3, Form an equation: the sum of two consecutive numbers is 41. Let the numbers be n and n + 1. Then 2n + 1 = 41, so 2n = 40 and n = 20. The numbers are 20 and 21.
Step 4, Perimeter problem: a rectangle's length is 4 more than its width w and its perimeter is 36. 2(w + w + 4) = 36, so 2w + 4 = 18, w = 7. Length is 11. Check: 2 x (7 + 11) = 36.
Step 5, Transposing: moving a term across the equals sign changes its sign. From 5y - 9 = 16 move -9 to get 5y = 25, so y = 5. This is the same as adding 9 to both sides.
Step 6, Your turn: solve 5x - 7 = 18, and form and solve: 4 times a number minus 6 equals 22. Answer: x = 5; and 4n - 6 = 22 gives 4n = 28, so n = 7.
Step 1, Complementary and supplementary: complementary angles add to 90 and supplementary add to 180. The complement of 38 is 90 - 38 = 52. The supplement of 125 is 180 - 125 = 55.
Step 2, Linear pair: two angles on a straight line are (3x + 10) and (2x + 20). They add to 180, so 5x + 30 = 180 and x = 30. The angles are 100 and 80. Check: 100 + 80 = 180.
Step 3, Vertically opposite angles: when two lines cross, opposite angles are equal. If one angle is 70, the one opposite is 70 and the two neighbours are 180 - 70 = 110 each.
Step 4, Parallel lines and a transversal: if one angle is 70, its corresponding angle is 70 and its alternate interior angle is 70. The co-interior (same side) angle is 180 - 70 = 110.
Step 5, Find an unknown: lines are parallel and a transversal makes alternate angles (4a + 10) and 50. Equal angles give 4a + 10 = 50, so 4a = 40 and a = 10. Check: 4 x 10 + 10 = 50.
Step 6, Your turn: two angles (2x + 15) and (x + 30) form a linear pair. Find x and the angles. Answer: 3x + 45 = 180, so x = 45; the angles are 105 and 75.
Step 1, Angle-sum property: a triangle has angles 40, 65 and x. The three add up to 180, so x = 180 - 40 - 65 = 75 degrees.

Step 2, Exterior angle: in triangle ABC with angles A = 50 and B = 60, the exterior angle at C equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles. So it is 50 + 60 = 110. Check: interior C is 70 and 70 + 110 = 180.
Step 3, Pythagoras property: in a right triangle with legs 6 and 8, hypotenuse squared = 36 + 64 = 100. So the hypotenuse is 10. The triple 6, 8, 10 is a scaled 3, 4, 5.
Step 4, Ladder problem: a 13 m ladder leans on a wall with its foot 5 m from the wall. Height squared = 169 - 25 = 144, so the height is 12 m. Check: 5, 12, 13 is a known triple.
Step 5, Test for a right triangle: sides 7, 24, 25. 7^2 + 24^2 = 49 + 576 = 625 and 25^2 = 625. The squares match, so the triangle is right-angled, with the right angle opposite 25.

Step 6, Your turn: find x in a triangle with angles x, 2x and 3x, and the other leg when the hypotenuse is 17 and one leg is 8. Answer: 6x = 180, x = 30; other leg is the root of 289 - 64 = 225, which is 15.
Step 1, SAS test: triangle ABC has AB = 5 cm, BC = 7 cm and angle B = 50. Triangle PQR has PQ = 5, QR = 7 and angle Q = 50. Two sides and the included angle match, so ABC is congruent to PQR by SAS.
Step 2, Use the match: with ABC congruent to PQR, corresponding parts are equal. So AC = PR, angle A = angle P, angle C = angle R. Write the correspondence in order, A to P, B to Q, C to R.
Step 3, SSS test: triangles with sides 4, 5, 6 and 6, 4, 5 are congruent by SSS because all three pairs of sides are equal. No angle information is needed.
Step 4, RHS test: two right triangles each have hypotenuse 10 cm and one leg 6 cm. They are congruent by RHS. The third side is the root of 100 - 36 = 64, so it is 8 cm in both.

Step 5, ASA and a failure: ASA needs two angles and the included side, such as angles 40 and 60 with the side 8 cm between them. But SSA (two sides and a non-included angle) is not enough, as different triangles can fit.

Step 6, Your turn: triangle one has angles 40 and 60 with the side between them 8 cm; triangle two has angles 60 and 40 with 8 cm between them. Are they congruent? Answer: yes, by ASA, and the third angle of each is 80.
Step 1, Parallelogram: base 12 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm. Area = base x height = 12 x 7 = 84 cm2. Use the height at right angles to the base, not the slanted side.
Step 2, Triangle: base 10 cm and height 6 cm. Area = 1/2 x 10 x 6 = 30 cm2. This is half of a parallelogram of the same base and height, 60 cm2.
Step 3, Circle with radius 7 cm using pi = 22/7: circumference = 2 x 22/7 x 7 = 44 cm. Area = 22/7 x 7 x 7 = 22 x 7 = 154 cm2. Check: 154 is a little less than the square of side 14 = 196.
Step 4, Circle from the diameter: diameter 20 cm gives radius 10 cm. With pi = 3.14, circumference = 3.14 x 20 = 62.8 cm and area = 3.14 x 100 = 314 cm2.
Step 5, Word problem: a circular park has radius 14 m. Area = 22/7 x 14 x 14 = 22 x 2 x 14 = 616 m2. Fencing the edge needs 2 x 22/7 x 14 = 88 m.
Step 6, Your turn: find the area of a parallelogram with base 9 cm and height 5 cm, and the circumference and area of a circle of radius 21 cm. Answer: 45 cm2; 132 cm and 1,386 cm2.
Step 1, Identify like terms: in 3x + 2y + 5x - 4y the x terms are 3x and 5x, and the y terms are 2y and -4y. Only like terms can be combined.
Step 2, Add: (3x + 2y) + (5x - 4y) = (3x + 5x) + (2y - 4y) = 8x - 2y. Group the like terms, then add their numbers.
Step 3, Subtract: (7a - 3b + 2) - (2a + b - 5). Change every sign in the second bracket: 7a - 3b + 2 - 2a - b + 5. Collect: 5a - 4b + 7.
Step 4, Find a value: for 3x^2 - 4x + 1 with x = 2, work 3 x 4 - 8 + 1 = 12 - 8 + 1 = 5. Square before multiplying by 3. Try x = -1 to see: 3 + 4 + 1 = 8.
Step 5, Use in a problem: a rectangle has length (2x + 3) and width x. Perimeter = 2(2x + 3 + x) = 6x + 6. If x = 4, the perimeter is 6 x 4 + 6 = 30. Direct check: 2 x (11 + 4) = 30.
Step 6, Your turn: add (4m + 3n) and (2m - 5n), and find 2a + 3b when a = 4 and b = -1. Answer: 6m - 2n; and 8 - 3 = 5.

Step 1, Nets: a cube net has 6 squares joined so that they fold into a closed box. A cuboid net has 6 rectangles, in 3 equal pairs. Fold test: a row of 4 squares with one square above and one below works.

Step 2, Count faces, vertices and edges: a cube has 6 faces, 8 vertices and 12 edges. Euler's check F + V - E = 2 gives 6 + 8 - 12 = 2. A triangular prism has 5 faces, 6 vertices and 9 edges: 5 + 6 - 9 = 2.

Step 3, Views: a stack has 3 cubes in the front row and 1 cube behind the left one. The front view shows 3 squares side by side and the top view shows 3 squares in a row plus 1 behind at the left end.
Step 4, Lines of symmetry: an equilateral triangle has 3, a regular hexagon has 6, a rectangle 2, and the letter H has 2 (one vertical, one horizontal). A scalene triangle has none.
Step 5, Check a net: a cross with 5 squares and 1 extra is a cube net only if no two squares overlap when folded. A row of 6 squares fails, since folding makes the end squares overlap.
Step 6, Your turn: find F + V - E for a square pyramid and say how many lines of symmetry a square has. Answer: 5 faces, 5 vertices, 8 edges gives 5 + 5 - 8 = 2; a square has 4 lines of symmetry.
Step 1, Solve 5x - 7 = 3x + 9. Move 3x to the left by subtracting it from both sides: 2x - 7 = 9. Add 7: 2x = 16. Divide by 2: x = 8.
Step 2, Check x = 8: left side 5 x 8 - 7 = 33, right side 3 x 8 + 9 = 33. Both sides equal 33, so x = 8 is correct. Always substitute into the original equation.
Step 3, With brackets: 3(x + 4) = 2x + 19. Expand the left side: 3x + 12 = 2x + 19. Subtract 2x: x + 12 = 19, so x = 7. Check: 3 x 11 = 33 and 2 x 7 + 19 = 33.
Step 4, With fractions: x/3 + 2 = x/2 - 1. Multiply every term by the LCM 6: 2x + 12 = 3x - 6. Then 12 + 6 = 3x - 2x, so x = 18. Check: 6 + 2 = 8 and 9 - 1 = 8.
Step 5, Word problem: a father is 3 times as old as his son. After 10 years he will be twice as old. With son's age x: 3x + 10 = 2(x + 10), so x = 10. Son 10, father 30. Check: 40 = 2 x 20.
Step 6, Your turn: solve 7x + 4 = 3x + 28. Answer: 4x = 24, so x = 6. Check: 7 x 6 + 4 = 46 and 3 x 6 + 28 = 46.
Step 1, Angle sum: a quadrilateral has angles 85, 95, 110 and x. The four angles add to 360, so x = 360 - 290 = 70 degrees. The sum 360 comes from splitting it into two triangles.
Step 2, Parallelogram angles: if angle A = 65, then opposite angle C = 65, and each adjacent angle is 180 - 65 = 115, so B = D = 115. Check: 65 + 115 + 65 + 115 = 360.
Step 3, Parallelogram diagonals: they bisect each other. If AC = 18 cm and BD = 14 cm, they meet at O with AO = 9 cm and BO = 7 cm. Opposite sides are equal and parallel.
Step 4, Rhombus: its diagonals are perpendicular and bisect each other. With diagonals 16 and 12, each half is 8 and 6, so a side is the root of 64 + 36 = 100, which is 10 cm. Perimeter 40 cm.
Step 5, Rectangle test: a rectangle's diagonals are equal. A parallelogram with sides 6 and 8 and diagonals both 10 is a rectangle, since 36 + 64 = 100 gives a right angle at the corner.
Step 6, Your turn: adjacent angles of a parallelogram are (2x + 10) and (3x - 20). Find x and the angles. Answer: 5x - 10 = 180, x = 38; the angles are 86 and 94.
Step 1, Pie chart angles: 600 students choose sports. Cricket 240, football 150, swimming 120, others 90. Cricket angle = 240 / 600 x 360 = 144 degrees. Football = 150 / 600 x 360 = 90.
Step 2, Finish and check: swimming = 120 / 600 x 360 = 72 degrees and others = 90 / 600 x 360 = 54. Sum 144 + 90 + 72 + 54 = 360. The angles must always add up to 360.
Step 3, Histogram: marks grouped as 0-10, 10-20, 20-30, 30-40 with frequencies 4, 9, 12, 5. Bars touch because the classes are continuous. The tallest bar, 20-30, holds 12 of the 30 students.
Step 4, Probability: a bag has 5 red, 3 blue and 2 green balls, 10 in all. P(blue) = 3/10. P(not red) = 5/10 = 1/2. Probabilities of all outcomes add to 1: 5/10 + 3/10 + 2/10 = 1.
Step 5, Die: P(prime) when rolling one die counts 2, 3, 5, so 3/6 = 1/2. P(a number greater than 4) counts 5 and 6, so 2/6 = 1/3. Probability is favourable outcomes divided by total outcomes.
Step 6, Your turn: of 40 students, 10 prefer tea; find its pie-chart angle, and P(even number) on a die. Answer: 10 / 40 x 360 = 90 degrees; P(even) = 3/6 = 1/2.
Step 1, Multiply two binomials: (2x + 3)(x - 4) = 2x(x) + 2x(-4) + 3(x) + 3(-4) = 2x^2 - 8x + 3x - 12 = 2x^2 - 5x - 12. Every term in one bracket meets every term in the other.
Step 3, Square of a difference: (5y - 3)^2 = 25y^2 - 30y + 9. Check with y = 1: 2^2 = 4 and 25 - 30 + 9 = 4. The middle term takes a minus sign.
Step 5, Find a missing term: x^2 + 10x + 25 is (x + 5)^2 since 2 x x x 5 = 10x and 5^2 = 25. Check with x = 1: 36 = 6^2.
Step 6, Your turn: expand (x + 7)(x - 7) and (4m + 1)^2. Answer: x^2 - 49; and 16m^2 + 8m + 1.
Step 1, Cube of side 5 cm: total surface area = 6 x side^2 = 6 x 25 = 150 cm2 and volume = 5^3 = 125 cm3. Six faces, each a square of area 25.
Step 2, Cuboid 8 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm: surface area = 2(lb + bh + hl) = 2(40 + 20 + 32) = 2 x 92 = 184 cm2. Volume = 8 x 5 x 4 = 160 cm3.
Step 3, Cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm, using pi = 22/7: curved surface = 2 x 22/7 x 7 x 10 = 440 cm2. Total surface = 2 x 22/7 x 7 x (7 + 10) = 44 x 17 = 748 cm2.
Step 4, Cylinder volume: pi r^2 h = 22/7 x 7 x 7 x 10 = 22 x 7 x 10 = 1,540 cm3. Check: the total surface 748 = 440 + 2 x 154 (two circular ends), and 440 + 308 = 748.
Step 5, Word problem: a cylindrical tank of radius 7 m and height 10 m holds 1,540 cubic metres. Since 1 cubic metre = 1,000 litres, it holds 1,540,000 litres.
Step 6, Your turn: find the volume and curved surface of a cylinder with radius 3.5 cm and height 8 cm. Answer: volume 22/7 x 12.25 x 8 = 308 cm3; curved surface 2 x 22/7 x 3.5 x 8 = 176 cm2.
Step 1, Common factor: 6x^2 + 9x. The HCF of 6 and 9 is 3 and both terms have x, so the common factor is 3x. Divide: 6x^2 / 3x = 2x and 9x / 3x = 3. Result: 3x(2x + 3).
Step 2, Factorise x^2 + 7x + 12: find two numbers that multiply to 12 and add to 7, which are 3 and 4. So (x + 3)(x + 4). Check by expanding: x^2 + 4x + 3x + 12 = x^2 + 7x + 12.
Step 3, Identities: x^2 - 49 = (x - 7)(x + 7) as a difference of squares. And 4x^2 - 12x + 9 = (2x - 3)^2, since 2 x 2x x 3 = 12x and 3^2 = 9.
Step 4, Plot y = 2x + 1. Table: x = -1 gives y = -1, x = 0 gives 1, x = 1 gives 3, x = 2 gives 5. Mark (-1, -1), (0, 1), (1, 3), (2, 5) and join them in a straight line.
Step 5, Read the graph: the line cuts the y-axis at 1 (the intercept) and rises 2 for each 1 across (slope 2). Check that the point (3, 7) lies on the line: 2 x 3 + 1 = 7.
Step 6, Your turn: factorise x^2 - 5x + 6 and find y for y = x - 2 at x = 3 and x = 0. Answer: (x - 2)(x - 3); and y = 1 at x = 3, and y = -2 at x = 0.
Step 1, Add polynomials: (3x^2 + 2x - 5) + (x^2 - 4x + 7). Group like terms: (3 + 1)x^2 + (2 - 4)x + (-5 + 7) = 4x^2 - 2x + 2. Degree stays 2.
Step 2, Multiply: (x + 3)(x^2 - 2x + 1) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x + 3x^2 - 6x + 3 = x^3 + x^2 - 5x + 3. Check at x = 2: left 5 x 1 = 5, right 8 + 4 - 10 + 3 = 5.
Step 3, Remainder theorem: divide p(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 - x + 5 by (x - 2). The remainder is p(2) = 8 + 8 - 2 + 5 = 19. No long division needed, just substitute the root of the divisor.
Step 4, Factor theorem: for p(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6, p(1) = 1 - 6 + 11 - 6 = 0, so (x - 1) is a factor. Dividing gives x^2 - 5x + 6, which factorises as (x - 2)(x - 3).
Step 5, Full factorisation: x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 = (x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3). Check p(2) = 8 - 24 + 22 - 6 = 0 and p(3) = 27 - 54 + 33 - 6 = 0. All three roots work.
Step 6, Your turn: find the remainder of x^3 - 3x^2 + 4 divided by (x - 1), and test whether (x - 2) is a factor. Answer: p(1) = 1 - 3 + 4 = 2; p(2) = 8 - 12 + 4 = 0, so yes.
Step 1, Plot points: A(3, 2) is 3 right and 2 up, in quadrant I. B(-4, 3) is in quadrant II, C(-2, -5) in quadrant III and D(5, -1) in quadrant IV. The x-coordinate is always read first.

Step 2, Distances from axes: for B(-4, 3) the distance from the y-axis is 4 (the abscissa without the sign) and the distance from the x-axis is 3 (the ordinate). A point on the x-axis looks like (a, 0).
Step 3, Rectangle: plot (1, 1), (5, 1), (5, 4), (1, 4). The length is 5 - 1 = 4 and the width is 4 - 1 = 3. Area = 4 x 3 = 12 square units. Perimeter = 14 units.
Step 4, Reflection: reflecting (3, 2) in the x-axis flips the sign of y, giving (3, -2). Reflecting in the y-axis gives (-3, 2). The point and its image are the same distance from the axis.
Step 5, Find a missing coordinate: the points (2, k) and (2, 7) lie on a vertical line x = 2. If the point is 3 units below the x-axis, then k = -3. Check: its distance from the x-axis is |-3| = 3.
Step 6, Your turn: name the quadrant of (-6, -2) and say where (0, -4) lies. Answer: quadrant III, with abscissa -6 and ordinate -2; (0, -4) lies on the y-axis, 4 units below the origin.
Step 1, Find solutions of x + y = 7: choose x and compute y. x = 0 gives y = 7; x = 2 gives y = 5; x = 7 gives y = 0. So (0, 7), (2, 5) and (7, 0) are solutions. There are infinitely many.
Step 2, Graph it: plot (0, 7), (2, 5), (7, 0) and draw the line through them. Check that (3, 4) lies on the line, since 3 + 4 = 7. Every point on the line is a solution.
Step 3, Write an equation: three pens cost x each and two notebooks cost y each, total 40. So 3x + 2y = 40. If x = 6 then 2y = 22, so y = 11. Check: 18 + 22 = 40.
Step 4, Translate a sentence: y is 3 more than twice x gives y = 2x + 3. Table: x = 0, y = 3; x = 1, y = 5; x = 2, y = 7. The points lie on a straight line.
Step 5, Special lines: the x-axis is y = 0 and the y-axis is x = 0. The line x = 3 is vertical through (3, 0). Write y - 4 = 0 as y = 4, a horizontal line through (0, 4).
Step 6, Your turn: find three solutions of 2x + 3y = 12. Answer: x = 0 gives y = 4; y = 0 gives x = 6; x = 3 gives y = 2. Check: 6 + 6 = 12.
Step 1, Use an axiom: things equal to the same thing are equal to each other. If AB = PQ and PQ = XY then AB = XY. So three stick lengths 12 cm, 12 cm, 12 cm are all equal.
Step 2, Equals added to equals: if x - 3 = 5 then x - 3 + 3 = 5 + 3, so x = 8. Each step of solving an equation uses an axiom like this one, which is why we say it is a logical argument.
Step 3, The whole and the part: a rope of length 10 m is cut so that a piece is 4 m. The whole (10) is greater than the part (4). That is Euclid's idea that the whole is greater than the part.
Step 4, Postulate: a straight line can be drawn between any two points. Through A and B there is exactly one such line. A theorem follows: two different lines cannot meet in more than one point.
Step 5, Midpoint: if C is the midpoint of AB and AB = 10 cm, then AC = CB = 5 cm. And if AB = CD for points A, B, C, D in order on a line, then AC = BD, since AC = AB + BC and BD = BC + CD.
Step 6, Your turn: name the axiom used to say that if a = b and b = c then a = c, and find AC when AB = 12 and C is the midpoint. Answer: things equal to the same thing are equal; AC = 6.
Step 1, Prove vertically opposite angles: lines AB and CD meet at O. Angle AOC + angle COB = 180 (linear pair) and angle COB + angle BOD = 180. So angle AOC = angle BOD.
Step 2, Use it: if angle AOC = 50 then angle BOD = 50 and angle COB = 130. Check: 50 + 130 = 180. The other vertically opposite pair is also 130 and 130.
Step 3, Parallel lines: lines AB and CD are parallel and a transversal makes an angle of 75. The alternate interior angle is 75 and the co-interior angle is 180 - 75 = 105.
Step 4, Solve for x: AB is parallel to CD and the alternate angles are (2x + 20) and (3x - 10). Setting them equal, 2x + 20 = 3x - 10, so x = 30. Each angle is 80. Check: 2 x 30 + 20 = 80.
Step 5, Triangle angle sum and exterior angle: in triangle ABC, angle A = 55 and angle B = 65, so angle C = 60. The exterior angle at C is 180 - 60 = 120, which equals 55 + 65.
Step 6, Your turn: the angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find them. Answer: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 parts, 180 / 9 = 20, so the angles are 40, 60 and 80.
Step 1, Isosceles proof: in triangle ABC, AB = AC and AD bisects angle A, meeting BC at D. In triangles ABD and ACD, AB = AC, angle BAD = angle CAD, and AD is common. So they are congruent by SAS.
Step 2, Conclusion: by congruence, BD = DC and angle B = angle C. So angles opposite equal sides are equal. If angle B is 70, then angle C is 70 and angle A is 180 - 140 = 40.
Step 3, Larger angle opposite longer side: in triangle with angles B = 70, C = 50, A = 60, the largest angle is B, so side AC is the longest. The smallest angle C = 50 faces the shortest side AB.
Step 4, Triangle inequality: sides 3, 4 and 8 cannot form a triangle since 3 + 4 = 7 is less than 8. Sides 6, 8 and 10 can, since 6 + 8 = 14 is greater than 10.
